card.title: Decompose
card.subtitle: break the passage into moves
card.status_plain: The moves for this passage exist (55 of them, with 25 connections). They were read from a retyped copy, not yet the checkout, so this is a worked example, honest about that.

what_it_is: Decompose breaks the checked-out passage into moves. A move is one action the text makes: an agent does an operation to something, with a result. It turns a block of text into an ordered list of small, labeled actions the rest of the method reads.
why_it_matters: The move is the unit the whole method works on, and it is where making the unsaid said begins. A gap is what a move leaves unsaid, so you cannot name a silence until you have named the moves it sits between. Every later step reads moves: the gaps hang off them, the later readings answer each move's question, the comparisons line moves up across texts. So the move boundary is load-bearing. Break the passage well and the reading holds. Break it badly and every step downstream inherits the error.

how_it_works.you give it: three things: the checked-out passage (the exact sourced text the Text step handed over), the one question you are reading it for (this decides what counts as important), and the year the text was written.
how_it_works.the method does: reads the passage sentence by sentence, marks each small action as a move, labels who does it, the operation, what it acts on, and the result, and records how the moves connect (one feeds the next, one reports another's speech).
how_it_works.you get back: an ordered list of moves, and the connections between them.

on_mark_16.what_counts_as_one_move: One move is one agent doing one operation to one thing, with one result. Start a new move when the agent changes, the operation changes, or the result changes. When in doubt, keep the move whole rather than splitting it: an under-split reading loses less than an over-split one.

the_anatomy_of_a_move.note: Every move has four slots: who does it, the operation, what it acts on, and the result. Here is the first move of Mark 16, fully labeled.

example.plain: Once the rest-day had ended, the three named women purchased aromatic spices intending to go and dress the body.
example.who: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome
example.result: spices in hand, with the intent to come and anoint him

worked_example.note: The opening of the passage, move by move, so you can see the text become a sequence of small labeled actions. These are the first 12 of 55 moves; the full list is the feed the reading room renders.

moves.plain: Once the rest-day had ended, the three named women purchased aromatic spices intending to go and dress the body.
moves.who: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome
moves.result: spices in hand, with the intent to come and anoint him

moves.plain: At daybreak on the week's first day they arrived at the burial place.
moves.result: their arrival at the tomb at sunrise

moves.plain: As they walked they were voicing a worry to one another.
moves.result: the question uttered aloud among them

moves.plain: They ask who will move the sealing-stone aside for them.
moves.on: the stone at the tomb's door

moves.plain: Aside from the narrator: the stone was of great size.
Raising their eyes, they perceived that the stone had already been shifted aside.
moves.operation: see (that the stone was rolled back)
moves.result: their perception that the stone is already moved

moves.plain: The stone had already been moved back from the opening.
Once inside the tomb, they saw a young figure seated to the right in a white robe.
moves.operation: see (a young man sitting on the right, dressed in white)
moves.on: M6a (the young man and his posture/attire)
moves.result: their perception of an unexpected occupant

moves.plain: A young figure was seated on the right side, wearing a white robe.
moves.who: not-stated (the young man is a topic, not a doer here)
moves.operation: sit (dressed in white, on the right)

moves.who: not-stated (they undergo it, not perform it)

moves.result: his utterance directed at the women

moves.plain: He orders them to stop being astonished.
moves.result: an imperative to release the fear

featured_moves.who: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome
featured_moves.result: spices in hand, with the intent to come and anoint him

featured_moves.result: the raising declared as accomplished; doer of the raising unnamed

featured_moves.result: the women away from the tomb

featured_moves.result: the commission un-executed; the news withheld

connections.plain: The 25 connections are of two kinds: 20 nesting (one move scopes over others, for example the young man's speech contains the announcement 'he has been raised') and 5 reporting (one move reports another's speech). Not every move links to another, so there are fewer connections than moves.

on_mark_16.the_silence_thread: Watch the pair M22 (the women flee the tomb) and M23 (they say nothing to anyone). The women are told to carry the resurrection news, and instead they say nothing. That silence is the ending the whole reading turns on. Follow this pair through every later step.

where_saved.plain: The moves save to the corpus, in the source_move table (one row per move), with their connections in source_move_edge. They join back to this passage through the same home the checkout opened: this passage's row in the text_checkout table (its id is gut-8268_016_v1), which you find by the method key MARK-16-WEB. So the moves, and every step built on them, sit in one findable place with the text they came from.

honest_limits: These moves were read from a retyped copy of the text, not yet from the library checkout, so the wording is a paraphrase. Re-run this step on the verbatim checkout text (a clean run on the real words rather than the retyped copy) and the moves refresh from the real words.
This is one coder on one pass, a reference reading, not a reliability-tested one yet.

crt.meta_line: Cold Read Test: PASS (2026-08-08). Two readers converged on orient and reproduce; a gap-scan closed five clarity bugs.

whats_next: Situate runs in parallel (the world the text came from). Together they feed the enriched move, and then the gaps: what the moves leave unsaid.

how_to_run.step 1, get the passage: Start from the checkout (the Text step, which hands over the exact sourced passage). Today the extractor reads a text file; a clean run on the verbatim checkout text feeds it the real words rather than the retyped copy.
how_to_run.step 2, extract the moves: ./scripts/_run_python.sh scripts/analysis/engine1_layer1_extract_moves.py --text <passage file> --source-key MARK-16-WEB --qud "What is the resurrection, and who transmits it?" --sitz-year 70
how_to_run.what each input means: --text is the passage to read. --source-key is the method key for this text (MARK-16-WEB), the same key that joins to the checkout home. --qud is the fixed Question Under Discussion (load-bearing: it decides what counts as salient). --sitz-year is the composition year.
how_to_run.step 4, where it saves: source_move (the moves) and source_move_edge (the connections), keyed on the method key, joined to the text_checkout home.
how_to_run.then: Situate runs in parallel; then the gaps.
